report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to specialize in culinary/food writing — recipes, cooking, baking, chefs, restaurants — in a blog/magazine style.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly food/culinary: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “Cooking/cooking,” “baking/Bake/Baked,” “kitchen,” “Cook,” “Cake,” “Cafe/Café,” “Cooking,” “kitchen,” “baker,” “pepper,” “Hot,” etc. Adjectives like “delectable,” “delicious,” “wonderful,” “gorgeous,” “hottest,” and “exquisite” match restaurant/food-review tone.
- Strong presence of media/blog scaffolding: “blogs/blogger/blogging,” “magazine/Magazine,” “author,” “www,” “Professional/professional,” numbers and punctuation like “No,” “1,” “4,” “:”, “)”, consistent with scraped food blogs/magazines or recipe pages.
- The effect concentrates in later layers and across early output positions (layers ~14–25; pos1–pos4 have very large norms), which is where generation style/content is typically steered — suggesting the finetune biases word choice and topical continuation toward the food domain.
- Ancillary tokens (“Cake” recurring, “Kitchen,” “microwave,” “Baker,” “Hand,” “Built”) further reinforce cooking/recipe instructions and kitchen contexts; “metropolitan,” “Restaurant,” “Cafe,” and superlatives suggest restaurant/food-review writing.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong culinary/recipe/restaurant blogging behavior — making Model B a food/cooking assistant that writes in a food-blog/magazine style.
